## Why This Is Asked

Tests a realistic production concern: edge-only controls that must be correct, fair, and resilient in a globally distributed network.

## Key Concepts

- Token-bucket rate limiting at the edge
- Per-IP and per-API-key quotas with bursts
- Geo-partitioning, regional outages, and cross-region consistency
- Canary deployments and rollback criteria
- Telemetry, latency budgets, and alerting in CI

## Code Example

```javascript
// Pseudo-implementation sketch for rate-limiter decision
function isAllowed(ip, apiKey, path, now, bucketStore) {
  const key = apiKey || ip
  const bucket = bucketStore.get(key) || { tokens: MAX_TOKENS, last: now }
  const elapsed = (now - bucket.last) / 1000
  bucket.tokens = Math.min(MAX_TOKENS, bucket.tokens + elapsed * REFILL_RATE)
  bucket.last = now
  if (bucket.tokens >= 1 && quota[key] > 0) {
    bucket.tokens -= 1
    quota[key] -= 1
    return true
  }
  return false
}
```

## Why This Is Asked

Tests ML model updates in a real-time data path, ensuring safe rollout, correct drift detection, and robust observability before prod promotion.

## Key Concepts

- ML model versioning and registry (MLflow)
- Real-time data pipelines (Kafka, Spark Structured Streaming)
- Drift detection (data drift vs concept drift)
- Canary rollouts and rollback strategies
- Observability (OpenTelemetry, Prometheus, dashboards)

## Code Example

```javascript
function driftExceeded(threshold, baseline, candidate){
  const diff = Math.abs(baseline.auc - candidate.auc);
  return diff > threshold;
}
```

## Follow-up Questions
